title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: PLAC absolute right vs most just judgment incoherence
pass_a_gloss: Placeus finishes the tip: what God does as judge he does by a law he laid down and the norm of justice; what he does by absolute right over creatures he does by free good pleasure, not by some prestablished law with justice demanding it—so absolute right and most just judgment do not sit well together in the imputation claim.
pass_b_english: For what God does as judge, he does according to a law laid down by himself and the norm of justice; but what he does as having absolute right over his creatures, he does by his most free good pleasure, not according to some law prestablished with justice demanding it.
source_text: Quae enim Deus facit ut judex, ea facit secundum latam a se legem & justitiae normam; quae vero facit ut absolutum habens in creaturas suas ius, ea facit pro liberrimo suo beneplacito, non autem secundum aliquam legem praestitutam, poscente justitia.
